chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The one in i'tikaf (seclusion in mosque) should not smell perfume, nor delight in basil (or pleasant scent), nor bargain, nor buy, nor sell. He said: Whoever performs i'tikaf for three days, on the fourth day he has the option: if he wishes, he adds more days, and if he wishes, he exits the mosque. But if he stays two days after the three, he does not exit the mosque until he completes three days. This report is predicated on the condition that he did not stipulate (a specific duration), because whoever is in such a state and stays two days, completing three days is obligatory upon him. And whoever stipulated (a specific duration), cancellation is permissible for him at any time he wishes, except that it is preferred for him, if two days have passed, to complete the three days. This indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for exiting or extending i'tikaf if no specific duration was stipulated?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the prohibition on commercial transactions and enjoying scents applies to the mu'takif, while the three-day rule serves as a default for those who did not stipulate a specific duration, allowing flexibility to exit or extend after two days. This narration highlights the Shia juristic distinction between stipulated (ishtirat) and non-stipulated i'tikaf, emphasizing that the obligation to complete three days is contingent upon the absence of a prior condition. It underscores the balance between spiritual devotion and practical ease in Islamic worship.
